content: GPU floating-point non-associativity (arXiv 2408.05148, cross-checked across V100/MI250X/GH200): reduction-order differences across GPU vendors/drivers are not just theoretical -- kernels using atomicAdd-style accumulation depend on warp-scheduler-determined order, different tensor-core MMA topologies per generation, and different approximations in special-function units, so 'the same' floating point computation on different hardware produces different low-order bits even with correct code on both sides. This means cross-hardware divergence is expected/inherent, not a bug -- the quantization step must tolerate this class of noise specifically, not try to eliminate it at the source.
